stack_spec.name: Built with Spec4 (BWS4)
stack_spec.description: A unified, self-hosted web app that showcases Spec4 through a gallery of illustrative example apps demonstrating agentic AI patterns: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool-use, a visual embeddings explorer, a single-call (simple vs. structured-output) demo, a two-step chained-calls (role-played writer/critic) demo, a plan-first planning-agent trip-day planner demo, an interleaved ReAct reason-act-observe search-loop demo presented as its deliberate counterpart, an orchestrated-subagents demo in which a coordinator picks two specialists from a fixed roster, briefs them, runs them in parallel and merges their answers, and a multi-agent collaboration demo in which a buyer agent and two rival seller agents holding sealed private constraints negotiate a competitive procurement award over A2A-shaped peer messages across a code-enforced opacity boundary.

languages.name: Python
languages.role: backend service — REST API, LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline, embeddings example app (embedding + PCA projection), single-call example app (simple/structured generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI), planning-agent example app (planner/executor agents with tool-calling via PydanticAI, SSE streaming), ReAct loop example app (hand-rolled bounded reason-act-observe loop with per-cycle PydanticAI typed calls, direct shared Exa search calls, semantic near-duplicate query guard, SSE streaming), orchestrated-subagents example app (coordinator delegation, concurrent knowledge-only specialists via asyncio.gather, merge, SSE streaming), multi-agent collaboration example app (A2A-shaped Pydantic protocol models, shared in-process peer message bus with slice-local opacity policy, deterministic RFQ composition, concurrent seller bid rounds, buyer counter/award turns, concurrent reveal and sensitivity explanation calls, SSE streaming), shared framework services (generation, embedding, storage, usage limiting, content moderation, peer message bus), Neon/Postgres access; from this revision run as a single always-on Uvicorn process under systemd on the project's own VPS

languages.name: TypeScript
languages.role: browser client — single-page app presenting the landing page and all example apps

targets.name: web_client
targets.purpose: the browser UI presenting the landing page and every example app (RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning-agent, ReAct loop, orchestrated-subagents, multi-agent collaboration, future patterns), with per-example-app code-splitting so the gallery can grow without bloating the initial load
targets.hosting: static files served directly by Caddy from the netcup VPS at the canonical public origin, same origin as the API
targets.build: Vite build producing a hashed static bundle with route-based lazy-loaded chunks per example app, built on the VPS by the deploy script (npm ci && npm run build) into dist/, which Caddy serves with SPA history fallback
targets.distribution: served at the app's root domain, the gallery's single canonical public address

exposure.transport: HTTPS only, with automatic Let's Encrypt certificate issuance and renewal by Caddy and automatic HTTP→HTTPS redirection

targets.name: api
targets.purpose: serves the SPA's data needs — LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline (chunking, embedding, retrieval), embeddings example app (preconfigured/custom text embedding and 2D projection), single-call example app (simple text and structured/schema-conforming generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI/OpenRouter), planning-agent example app (planner call, plan validation, tool-using executor calls streamed via server-sent events), ReAct loop example app (custom-question suitability check, the bounded interleaved reason-act-observe loop with per-cycle typed model calls and direct Exa searches, run-record persistence and retrieval, hop-source annotation, all streamed via server-sent events), orchestrated-subagents example app (moderation gate, coordinator delegation decision, two concurrent knowledge-only specialists, merged answer, all streamed via server-sent events), multi-agent collaboration example app (deterministic RFQ composition, two concurrent seller bid rounds, buyer counter and award turns, concurrent reveal/sensitivity explanation calls, A2A-shaped peer messages delivered over the shared in-process bus with code-enforced opacity, NegotiationRecord persistence, all streamed via server-sent events), Exa search integration, and shared framework services (generation, embedding, storage, usage limiting, content moderation, peer message bus)
targets.runtime: Python 3.12 under Uvicorn as a single always-on process (--workers 1, async concurrency only — never multiple workers, because torch/sentence-transformers, the fitted PCA projection, the in-process peer message bus and the ReAct duplicate-guard cache are all per-process state) on a netcup VPS 500 G12 (2 vCores, 4 GB DDR5 ECC RAM, 128 GB NVMe, always-on); the FastAPI lifespan warm-up loads the embedding model and fits the 2D projection once at boot and stays warm for the lifetime of the process, and remains best-effort so a failed projection fit still boots
targets.hosting: self-hosted on the project's netcup VPS 500 G12, supervised by systemd (Restart=always, enabled at boot, EnvironmentFile on a root-owned 0600 file outside the repository), fronted by Caddy which reverse-proxies /api/* to Uvicorn on localhost
targets.build: uv sync on the VPS from the repo's pyproject.toml/uv.lock, followed by uv run alembic upgrade head, then systemctl restart of the service unit
targets.api_contract: REST; OpenAPI schema auto-generated by FastAPI; the planning-agent run endpoint streams incremental JSON results (Plan, then StepResults, then Itinerary) as server-sent events over a POST request; the ReAct loop run endpoint streams one JSON envelope per event type (run_started, cycle_thought, cycle_action, cycle_observation, cycle_counter, final_answer, budget_exhausted, error) as server-sent events over a POST request, with the completed trace also retrievable via GET /api/react/run/{run_id}; the orchestrated-subagents run endpoint likewise streams the DelegationDecision, then per-specialist status/answer events as the concurrent specialist tasks complete, then the MergedAnswer; the multi-agent collaboration run endpoint streams one event per negotiation stage (QuotationRequest, per-seller opening bid events as the concurrent bids complete, CounterOffers, per-seller best-and-final bid events, Award, then the reveal and sensitivity panels as their concurrent explanation calls complete), all as server-sent events over a POST request; every route, payload and streaming behaviour is unchanged by this revision's hosting migration

exposure.transport: HTTPS only, terminated by Caddy at the edge with automatic Let's Encrypt certificates; Uvicorn itself binds only to localhost and is never directly reachable from the network
exposure.cors: allow only the single non-wildcard configured browser origin (CORS_ORIGIN), retained unchanged as part of the environment contract; because the SPA is now served from the same canonical origin as the API, cross-origin requests no longer occur in production and the policy is exercised chiefly in local development

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model for grounded, structured-output answers (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/tool-oriented output (google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free)
a capable general-purpose free model able to produce both plain text and JSON-schema-conforming structured output for a single direct prompt/response demo (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/JSON output, for the single-call demo

OpenRouter (via LiteLLM).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via LiteLLM routing if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model's rate limit is hit or it errors, for both the RAG and single-call tiers

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model able to sustain a distinct role-played persona (struggling writer, harsh critic) across a two-step sequential chain (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at persona/role-played and structured JSON output, for the chained-calls demo

a capable free model with reliable native tool-calling and structured output, able to decompose a trip goal into a validated small plan and to execute research/synthesis steps against a web-search tool
a fast alternate free model, also capable of tool-calling and structured JSON output, for the planner and executor calls

a capable free model with reliable typed/structured output able to emit, per cycle, a short thought plus a discriminated action — either the exact search query to issue or the decision that it can now answer — reading each new observation from the loop's assembled context; no native tool-calling is required of it because the search is executed by application code between cycles
a fast alternate free model, also reliable at typed thought/action output, for any cycle of the ReAct loop or its final-answer call

a capable free model with reliable typed output producing a suitability verdict for a visitor's own question — whether it chains two or more facts, whether it needs live information, an estimated hop count and a confidence — so a single-hop or unanswerable free-form question is flagged before the loop spends its budget
a fast alternate free model with reliable typed output, for the custom-question suitability check

a capable free model with reliable typed output producing, after a run completes, the per-hop source annotation — for each fact the answer rests on, whether it came from an observation in the trace or from the model's own parametric knowledge, and which cycle supplied it — so the overview's teaching point about where observation was genuinely required is grounded in the run's own trace rather than asserted
a fast alternate free model with reliable typed output, for the post-run hop-source annotation call

a capable general-purpose free model with reliable structured output, able to (a) choose exactly two specialists from a fixed roster of four and write a distinct brief for each, (b) answer a briefed sub-question as a knowledge-only specialist with no tool access, and (c) merge two independent specialist answers into one integrated response
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured JSON output, for the coordinator delegation call, either specialist call, or the merge call

structured-output generation of the disagreement note comparing the two specialist answers; produced as fields on the merge call's existing structured output rather than as an additional model call, so the run's three-call budget is unchanged

a capable free model with reliable structured output, able to sustain a private-constraint-bound negotiating persona across bid → counter → best-and-final turns without disclosing its sealed position, and to award a deal with a rationale weighed explicitly against the visitor's stated priority weighting

a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured JSON output and persona adherence, for any of the six negotiation turns (either seller's opening bid, the buyer's counter-offers, either seller's best-and-final bid, the buyer's award)

a capable free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, producing the end-of-run private-position reveal explanation for each party — why a seller held firm or conceded on a given axis, read against its now-unsealed constraints; a dedicated thin-schema call rather than extra fields on the award call, so a conformance failure degrades only the reveal panel and never the award payload
a fast alternate free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, for the private-position reveal explanation call

a capable free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, producing the counterfactual priority-sensitivity explanation — whether a different priority weighting would have changed the winner and why; a dedicated call because asking the award turn to both decide and reason counterfactually about its own decision in one shot is an unreliable prompt
a fast alternate free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, for the priority-sensitivity explanation call

OpenRouter (via PydanticAI).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via PydanticAI's native FallbackModel if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model errors or hits its rate limit — for either step of the chained-calls chain, for any planner or executor call of the planning-agent run, for any per-cycle thought/action call, the final-answer call, the custom-question suitability check or the post-run hop-source annotation of the ReAct loop run, for the coordinator delegation call, either specialist call, or the merge call of the orchestrated-subagents run, and for any of the six negotiation turns or either of the two explanation calls of the multi-agent collaboration run; all slugs are read from the same shared ordered free-tier model chain in model_registry.py used by the LiteLLM lane

integrations.name: Exa Search API
integrations.purpose: fetch ranked, real external search results (title, summary/snippet, source) so tool-use example apps can incorporate outside information, serve as the model-invoked web-search tool for the planning-agent example app's research steps, and serve as the observation source for each act step of the ReAct loop example app, where the exact query the model chose is issued verbatim and its returned snippets are rendered as the cycle's observation
integrations.auth: API key; EXA_API_KEY, now read from the systemd EnvironmentFile on the VPS rather than the Render dashboard, and never committed to the repository

integrations.name: OpenAI Moderation API (omni-moderation-latest)
integrations.purpose: pre-dispatch safety classification of visitor-supplied free-form questions (abuse, self-harm, sexual, hate, violence, illicit) before any coordinator call is made; chosen because the moderation endpoint is free of charge and does not consume the OpenRouter free-model allowance, so the orchestrated-subagents run's three-model-call budget is unaffected; exposed as a shared framework service so any future example app with a free-form input can reuse it, and invoked only for free-form input — curated preset questions are pre-vetted and skip it entirely; the ReAct loop example app reuses this same shared service for its free-form visitor questions before the suitability check, and its five curated presets bypass it; the multi-agent collaboration example app has no free-text input at all (scenario enum plus a numeric weighting vector) and therefore never calls it
integrations.protocol: REST over HTTPS; POST /v1/moderations, called with httpx and parsed into a Pydantic ModerationVerdict
integrations.auth: API key; OPENAI_API_KEY, now read from the systemd EnvironmentFile on the VPS rather than the Render dashboard, and never committed to the repository

primary_store.purpose: durable relational store for everything the app writes, doubling as the vector index for the RAG example app; remains external and managed on Neon after the move to the self-hosted VPS, so the migration changes nothing about where the gallery's information lives
primary_store.durability: source of truth; survives restarts, redeploys and the host migration itself, because it is external to the VPS; Neon's free tier persists indefinitely

collections.name: stored_records
collections.purpose: the shared storage abstraction's generic key-addressed retention records, used by apps that need to keep or retrieve small pieces of information through the shared retention capability rather than a slice-specific table

collections.name: usage_limits
physical: usage window column keyed to the current UTC hour, plus the per-UTC-day cap window
collections.purpose: the showcase-wide model/search allowance gate, enforced server-side before every provider call by every example app, windowed per UTC hour and per UTC day; the multi-agent collaboration example app's runs-per-hour limit is this existing framework-standard gate rather than a tightened per-app counter, and the ReAct loop app's every model call and every Exa search is accounted here as well; unchanged by the hosting migration, which is behaviour-preserving with respect to every usage cap

collections.name: allowance_holds
collections.purpose: reserve/redeem/refund records against the showcase-wide hourly usage gate, so a run's full call budget is held before its first model call and a confirmed dispatch either completes or is refused up front with a clear reason; the orchestrated-subagents run holds three calls before the coordinator delegation call, and the multi-agent collaboration run holds all eight (six negotiation plus two explanation) before the deterministic RFQ is composed; the ReAct loop run holds its full worst-case ceiling (up to 8 search-cycle calls plus 1 final-answer call plus the post-run annotation call) before the first cycle, and refunds the unspent remainder when the loop answers early; refunded when a run fails before spending its reserved calls
physical: index on capability and usage window

collections.name: moderation_log
collections.purpose: safety-gate telemetry for free-form question moderation: a salted hash of the question (never the raw text), the returned category, confidence, latency, and whether the call failed closed; satisfies the capability's privacy requirement that raw visitor question text is not retained
physical: salted question hash column; no raw question text column

collections.name: negotiation_runs
collections.purpose: the immutable per-run negotiation record header written at run end: the selected scenario id and priority weighting, the deterministically composed RequestForQuotation, both rounds of bids, the buyer's counter-offers, the award with its priority references, the reveal and sensitivity explanation payloads, per-stage timings, model_calls_used, and degradation flags for any stage that failed or returned non-conforming output; stage payloads are held as JSONB while the header columns carry the queryable telemetry the capability's eval signal needs
physical: negotiation_stage_call_count and total_model_calls_used columns (queryable, not buried in JSONB)
JSONB columns for the RFQ, opening bids, counter-offers, final bids, award, reveal and sensitivity payloads

collections.name: peer_messages
collections.purpose: one row per A2A-shaped peer message exchanged during a run, foreign-keyed to negotiation_runs, so the chronological sender-to-recipient message log is a stored projection rather than a client-side tally and the app's headline opacity claim is provable from the store: seller_to_seller_count is a single SQL predicate over sender and recipient, expected to be zero for every run
physical: sender and recipient columns (indexed together, so seller-to-seller traffic is queryable)
JSONB work-item column carrying the A2A-shaped Task/Message/Artifact payload

collections.name: react_runs
collections.purpose: the per-run ReAct trace record written at run end and read back whole by GET /api/react/run/{run_id}: the ordered cycles (thought, action kind, exact query issued, observation snippets or explicit empty-result flag), the terminal card (final answer with the observations it drew on, or budget-exhausted with what remained unresolved), the custom-question suitability verdict where one was made, and the post-run hop-source annotations
physical: id (primary, the run_id used by the retrieval route)

queryable header columns: question_origin (preset id or 'custom'), searches_used, cycle_budget, ending ('final_answer' | 'budget_exhausted'), duplicate_queries_blocked, empty_observations, suitability_verdict fields (chained_facts, needs_live_info, estimated_hops, confidence), annotation_outcome
JSONB ordered cycle-trace column (thought, action_kind, query_text, observation snippets, is_empty, status per cycle)

collections.name: service_log_entries
collections.purpose: the shared framework services' per-call service log: which capability was invoked, by which example app, its outcome and its usage accounting, written for every generation, embedding, search and moderation call across the gallery

embedding_projection_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of preconfigured embeddings + fitted PCA model, held in memory (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors, scikit-learn PCA), loaded and fitted once in the FastAPI lifespan at boot
embedding_projection_cache.purpose: fills the vector_index substrate for the embeddings example app's custom_text_semantic_placement capability: holds the preconfigured examples' embeddings and the fitted PCA projection so a new custom-text point can be transformed into the same stable 2D layout without recomputing it, and without persisting user-entered custom text beyond the request; on the always-on VPS this state is built once at boot and stays warm for the whole lifetime of the single Uvicorn process, which is what removes the first-visit warm-up penalty the previous host imposed on every cold start
embedding_projection_cache.durability: ephemeral in-process derived state, rebuildable from bundled_assets' preconfigured_text_examples and never a source of truth; built once at boot on the always-on host and retained for the lifetime of the process, so it is re-paid only on an explicit deploy restart rather than on visitor traffic; custom text embeddings exist only for the duration of the request and are never persisted

collections.name: preconfigured_example_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) per preconfigured example
fitted PCA model held in memory, reused via .transform() for custom text

react_query_guard_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of the current run's issued-query embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via the shared sentence-transformers service), held for the lifetime of one run
react_query_guard_cache.purpose: backs the semantic near-duplicate query guard: each candidate query the model chooses is embedded and cosine-compared against the queries already issued in this run, so a rephrased repeat is blocked before it spends a search and the loop cannot burn its budget circling the same question; scoped to a single run because duplicate detection is only ever meaningful within one trace, and held in process because the shared embedding service spends no third-party quota
react_query_guard_cache.durability: ephemeral — exists only for the duration of one run and is discarded when the run ends; not a source of truth and never persisted, so a visitor's question text is not retained by the guard

collections.name: issued_query_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) per query issued so far in the run
cosine-similarity comparison against a tuned duplicate threshold

bundled_assets.choice: static content bundled at build time
bundled_assets.purpose: read-only content that only changes via a code change/redeploy, not user action

collections.name: example_app_directory
collections.purpose: the single shared description of available example apps from which both the landing-page roster and the persistent hamburger navigation are drawn, so an example cannot appear in one and not the other

collections.name: preconfigured_text_examples
collections.purpose: the curated set of words, short phrases, and sentences spanning multiple categories used to seed the embeddings example app's plot

collections.name: preset_prompts
collections.purpose: the curated set of example prompts (e.g. summarize, classify, extract) with their labeled intent, offered as one-click choices in the single-call example app

collections.name: persona_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates and few-shot exemplars defining the 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' personas used by the two chained calls; read-only, versioned in-repo

collections.name: planning_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the planning-agent example app: the planner prompt (goal decomposition into a bounded, validated plan of research + synthesis steps) and the synthesis prompt (composing the final one-day itinerary from step results); read-only, versioned in-repo

collections.name: specialist_roster_config
collections.purpose: the fixed roster of four knowledge-only specialists (Technical, Financial, Historical, Practical) with each one's id, display name, scope description, and column colour; read as the closed set the coordinator must choose exactly two from, and used to validate the delegation decision before it is shown to the visitor

collections.name: curated_presets
collections.purpose: curated preset questions, each with a preset id and its wording, chosen so different presets produce visibly different specialist pairings; preset questions are pre-vetted and therefore bypass the moderation gate that free-form questions pass through

collections.name: orchestration_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the orchestrated-subagents example app: the coordinator delegation prompt, the specialist prompt, and the merge prompt; read-only, versioned in-repo

collections.name: procurement_scenario_catalog
collections.purpose: the pre-tuned procurement scenarios and the selectable priority weightings for the multi-agent collaboration example app: per scenario, the goods description, the buyer's baseline requirements and BATNA, and the negotiable term axes; authored as version-controlled typed Python literals so mypy strict checks these deeply nested fixtures

collections.name: sealed_private_constraints
collections.purpose: per scenario and per seller, the hidden negotiating position — cost floor, capacity ceiling, delivery capability, warranty liability limit — plus the reveal headline and explanation seed used by the end-of-run unsealing; authored as typed Python literals, with sealing enforced by the message bus's opacity policy at access time

collections.name: agent_identity_cards
collections.purpose: the three A2A-shaped identity cards (buyer plus two rival sellers) published for inspection before or during a run: name, provider organisation, declared skills, declared capabilities, and explicit tool_access of none

collections.name: collaboration_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the multi-agent collaboration example app: the seller opening-bid and best-and-final prompts, the buyer counter-offer prompt, the buyer award prompt, and the two thin-schema explanation prompts; read-only, versioned in-repo

collections.name: react_preset_catalog
collections.purpose: the five curated multi-hop preset questions for the ReAct loop example app, with maintainer-authored metadata per preset: the expected hop facts, which hops require observation, why each hop defeats memorised knowledge, and whether the preset is one of the three guaranteed fully-observed demonstrations; stores questions ONLY and never answers, so time-variable answers self-refresh from live search on every run

collections.name: react_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the ReAct loop example app: the per-cycle reason/action prompt, the final-answer prompt, the custom-question suitability prompt, and the post-run hop-source annotation prompt; read-only, versioned in-repo

collections.name: educational_overviews
collections.purpose: the per-app short educational overview content — pattern explanation, quota rationale, and cross-references between the plan-first Planning Agent app and the interleaved ReAct Loop app; unchanged by this revision, since the hosting migration is behaviour-preserving with respect to all visitor-facing messaging

browser_local_storage.purpose: keeps small per-device visitor state across visits without a backend round trip, and keeps each example app's own demonstration run counter and prior results on the device so they survive navigating away and back
browser_local_storage.durability: persists per-device/browser only; not a source of truth, not shared across devices; resettable by the visitor — hard quota protection is always the server-side usage_limits gate plus per-run call ceilings, never this store

collections.name: theme_preference
collections.purpose: the visitor's chosen light/dark theme

collections.name: run_allowance
collections.purpose: advisory per-session run counter and cap for the planning-agent example app, shown to the user with remaining runs; deliberately client-side only — hard quota protection remains the server-side usage_limits gate plus the fixed per-run call ceiling enforced by plan validation

collections.name: orchestrated_run_allowance
collections.purpose: the orchestrated-subagents example app's three-run session counter plus the visitor's own prior run records (delegation decision, per-specialist briefs, specialist answers, merged answer), stamped with the UTC hour so the counter resets on the same hourly clock as the server-side showcase-wide gate

collections.name: last_negotiation_run
collections.purpose: a cache of the visitor's most recent multi-agent collaboration run so the negotiation record, reveal and message log rehydrate instantly on returning to the app without a server round trip; layered over the authoritative negotiation_runs/peer_messages persistence rather than replacing it

collections.name: react_run_allowance
collections.purpose: the ReAct loop example app's two-run session counter — the gallery's tightest per-app limit — plus the run_id and rendered trace of the visitor's own prior runs, stamped with the UTC hour so the counter resets on the same clock as the server-side showcase-wide gate; the stored run_id lets the full trace be re-fetched from GET /api/react/run/{run_id} rather than trusting the cached copy

chunking_pipeline.choice: hand-rolled paragraph/fixed-window text splitter, in application code
chunking_pipeline.purpose: splits reference_dataset documents into passages before embedding; kept simple and transparent given the small curated dataset, serving the project's teaching-clarity goal

embedding_pipeline.choice: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), in-process at index time and query time, loaded once in the FastAPI lifespan at boot on the always-on VPS
embedding_pipeline.purpose: fills the catalog's embedding_pipeline substrate for the RAG example (vectors written to and read from dataset_embeddings), the embeddings example app (vectors for preconfigured examples and custom text, held in embedding_projection_cache), and the ReAct loop's semantic near-duplicate query guard — one shared model, never a second one; on the self-hosted always-on instance the model load happens once at boot and stays resident for the process's lifetime, so no visitor ever pays the load cost, and the 4 GB of guaranteed RAM removes the memory pressure the previous host's free tier imposed; the package itself is listed under libraries

retriever.choice: SQLAlchemy query using pgvector's cosine-distance operator against dataset_embeddings
retriever.purpose: finds the top-N passages most similar to a question's embedding, to ground the generated answer

pipeline_runner.choice: PydanticAI, using its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel to run the fixed two-step 'struggling writer' → 'harsh critic' sequence, with the first call's response passed directly as the second call's input
pipeline_runner.purpose: fills the catalog's pipeline_runner substrate for the chained-calls example app; the free-model slugs used by its OpenRouterProvider and FallbackModel are read from the same shared model-slug config module the LiteLLM lane uses, and the existing usage_limits/service_log_entries quota-check function gates calls on this path exactly as it gates the LiteLLM path

agent_loop_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agent runs (OpenRouterProvider + FallbackModel, slugs from the shared model-slug config) in two deliberately different control shapes: (a) for the planning-agent example app, one structured-output planner call produces a Pydantic-validated Plan capped at 2–3 executor steps, then executor steps run sequentially only after the user's explicit go-ahead; (b) for the ReAct loop example app, a hand-rolled bounded while-loop in backend/app/react/ owns the iteration — each cycle is one PydanticAI call returning a validated ReactStep (short thought plus a discriminated action, either search(query) or answer), the slice executes the search between cycles, appends the observation to the assembled context, advances the cycle counter, and terminates on either the model's answer decision or the ~8-search ceiling; in both shapes the shared usage-limit gate is checked before every model call and each result is streamed to the client as it completes
agent_loop_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's agent_loop_runtime substrate for the planning-agent and ReAct loop example apps; the ReAct loop is hand-rolled so the cycle count is a code invariant allowance_holds can reserve against, every cycle boundary is a first-class SSE emission point, and the near-duplicate query guard can run between the model's chosen query and the search being issued; the PydanticAI package itself is listed under libraries

tool_execution_harness.choice: two fillings of the same substrate, per app: (a) for the planning-agent example app, PydanticAI native tool-calling (tool registration on the executor agent) wrapping the existing Exa search client (httpx) as a typed web-search tool for research steps; (b) for the ReAct loop example app, a direct in-process call from the loop's act step to the shared Exa wrapper at backend/app/services/web_search.py — no tool registration, no MCP — with the semantic near-duplicate guard interposed before the call and the verbatim result snippets returned as the cycle's observation
tool_execution_harness.purpose: fills the catalog's tool_execution_harness substrate for the planning-agent and ReAct loop example apps; in both apps the run-allowance/quota check is a direct internal service-layer call, never a model-exposed tool, so the model cannot decide whether quota is spent; the PydanticAI and httpx packages themselves are listed under libraries

subagent_orchestration_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agents dispatched directly in-process and fanned out with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True): one structured-output coordinator agent returns a Pydantic-validated DelegationDecision (exactly two specialist ids from the fixed four-name roster, a pairing rationale, and a distinct brief per specialist), then after the visitor's explicit dispatch confirmation the two knowledge-only specialist agents run as concurrent async tasks, then the coordinator agent is called a third time to merge their answers
subagent_orchestration_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's subagent_orchestration_runtime substrate for the orchestrated-subagents example app; dispatching in application code rather than via a model-driven tool loop is what guarantees exactly three calls and keeps the specialists genuinely parallel, which is the visible lesson of the demo; gathering with return_exceptions=True is what lets one specialist fail while the other column's answer stays on screen; the PydanticAI package itself is listed under libraries

agent_message_bus.choice: hand-rolled in-process message bus as a shared framework service at backend/app/services/message_bus.py — an append-only ordered envelope store with deliver(message), context_for(agent_id) filtering strictly on recipient equality, and a chronological log projection — with a slice-local opacity policy layer in the collaboration app applying the buyer/seller roles, sealed-constraint access rules and the no-seller-to-seller invariant on top of it
agent_message_bus.purpose: fills the catalog's agent_message_bus substrate for the multi-agent collaboration example app, delivering each peer Message and assembling every agent turn's context from only the messages addressed to that agent, so peer opacity is enforced structurally in code rather than by prompt instruction; being in-process state, it is one more reason the API runs as a single Uvicorn process rather than multiple workers; injected via FastAPI Depends so tests can substitute it

protocol_runtime.choice: hand-rolled A2A-shaped Pydantic models in the collaboration slice (backend/app/collab/protocol.py): AgentCard with AgentProvider/AgentSkill/AgentCapabilities, Task with TaskStatus/TaskState, Message with Role and Part/DataPart, and Artifact — serialised camelCase per the A2A spec's convention, carried over the shared in-process message bus with no HTTP, JSON-RPC or gRPC transport binding
protocol_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's protocol_runtime substrate for the multi-agent collaboration example app: implements A2A's Layer 1 canonical data model and Layer 2 interaction pattern while deliberately omitting Layer 3 transport bindings, exactly as the vision constrains; the overview says plainly that the exchanges are modelled on A2A's data model and interaction pattern rather than claiming the protocol's own objects, and states what a real cross-owner deployment would add

tls_termination_and_static_serving.choice: Caddy 2 on the netcup VPS, serving the Vite dist/ bundle as static files with SPA history fallback and reverse-proxying /api/* to Uvicorn on localhost, with automatic Let's Encrypt certificate issuance and renewal and automatic HTTP→HTTPS redirection; configured by a single Caddyfile in the repo's deploy/ directory
tls_termination_and_static_serving.purpose: gives the gallery one canonical public HTTPS origin that visitors' browsers trust, with certificate renewal built into the server rather than delegated to an external timer, so an expired certificate is structurally hard rather than merely automated; serving the SPA and the API from the same origin also removes cross-origin traffic from production entirely while the CORS_ORIGIN contract is retained unchanged; Caddy's proxy defaults do not buffer responses, which is what keeps the four server-sent-event example apps streaming progressively through the edge

process_supervision.choice: systemd service unit on the netcup VPS running a single Uvicorn process (--workers 1) under uv, with Restart=always, enabled at boot, and EnvironmentFile pointing at a root-owned 0600 secrets file outside the repository; logs to the journal alongside structlog's JSON output; Caddy runs under its own packaged unit
process_supervision.purpose: replaces the retired managed platform's process lifecycle: keeps the always-on instance running across crashes and reboots so the boot-time embedding-model load and PCA projection fit stay warm for the process's lifetime, and holds the carried-over environment contract (DATABASE_URL, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, CORS_ORIGIN, optional SENTRY_DSN/VITE_SENTRY_DSN) in a file the repository never sees; a single worker is mandatory rather than incidental, because the loaded model, the fitted projection, the in-process peer message bus and the ReAct duplicate-guard cache are all per-process state

release_delivery.choice: a shell deploy script in the repo's deploy/ directory, run on the VPS: git pull → uv sync → npm ci && npm run build → uv run alembic upgrade head → systemctl restart of the service unit; Node 20 and uv are installed on the host so the frontend bundle is built in place
release_delivery.purpose: replaces the retired managed platform's build-and-deploy pipeline with one readable, version-controlled procedure that documents the entire release in a single file; the quality gates (ruff, mypy, pytest, vitest) remain developer-run before push, as they are today, since no CI exists in the tree and adding one is out of this revision's scope; a release is a brief restart during which the warm state is rebuilt at boot, so updates are deliberate and infrequent rather than hot-swapped

ai_conventions.prompt_versioning: every prompt-bearing slice stores its templates as versioned files in-repo under backend/app/<slice>/prompts/, tagged with a semantic version in the filename/header and loaded by a thin resolver function, with the corresponding structured-output schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models: rag/ (answer_v1.md), single_call/ (presets plus per-preset schema models), chained_calls/ (writer_v1.md, critic_v1.md), planning/ (planner_v1.md, synthesis_v1.md with the Plan/StepResult/Itinerary schemas), orchestrated/ (delegation_v1.md, specialist_v1.md, merge_v1.md with the DelegationDecision/Brief/SubagentResult/MergedAnswer schemas, the merged answer carrying the disagreement note as fields on the same schema), collab/ (seller_bid_v1.md, seller_final_v1.md, buyer_counter_v1.md, buyer_award_v1.md, reveal_explanation_v1.md, sensitivity_v1.md with the Bid/CounterOffer/Award and two narrow explanation schemas), and react/ (cycle_v1.md, final_answer_v1.md, suitability_v1.md, hop_annotation_v1.md with the ReactStep/FinalAnswer/SuitabilityVerdict/HopAnnotation schemas); schemas are deliberately kept narrow per call so a non-conforming response degrades only its own panel; no external prompt-management tool. Unchanged by this revision's hosting migration.

project_structure.purpose: the self-hosted deployment artifacts introduced this revision: the Caddyfile (single canonical origin, static dist/ serving with SPA history fallback, /api/* reverse proxy to Uvicorn on localhost, automatic Let's Encrypt TLS), the systemd service unit template for the Uvicorn process (Restart=always, boot-enabled, EnvironmentFile referencing a root-owned 0600 secrets file outside the repo), the deploy shell script (git pull, uv sync, npm ci && npm run build, alembic upgrade head, systemctl restart), and a README documenting first-time VPS provisioning; render.yaml is deleted from the repo root as the previous host is retired entirely

thin FastAPI routers, one module per feature (landing, RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning-agent, ReAct loop, orchestrated-subagents, multi-agent collaboration, shared services, health)

thin SSE router for the multi-agent collaboration run: validates the scenario enum and priority weighting, delegates to the slice service, and streams one event per negotiation stage plus the two explanation panels

thin router for the ReAct loop example app: POST run streaming the per-cycle SSE envelopes (opening its own DB session inside the generator, never via Depends), GET run/{run_id} returning the persisted trace, and GET presets returning the five curated questions with their display metadata but never any stored answers

shared framework services: LLM access (LiteLLM wrapper), embedding (sentence-transformers wrapper), Exa web search, storage abstraction, shared model-slug config/model registry, and the usage-limit quota-check/logging function with reserve/redeem/refund holds

shared content-moderation service: a generic moderate(text, calling_context) -> ModerationVerdict function calling the OpenAI moderation endpoint over httpx with tenacity-bounded retry, failing closed with a plain-language visitor message, logging only a salted hash of the input, and injected via FastAPI Depends

shared in-process peer message bus: append-only ordered envelope store with deliver(message), context_for(agent_id) filtering strictly on recipient equality, and a chronological log projection; injected via FastAPI Depends so tests can substitute it

FastAPI app entrypoint: router registration, CORS middleware pinned to the single configured origin, Sentry wiring, and the lifespan warm-up that loads the embedding model and fits the 2D projection once at boot — best-effort by design so a failed fit still boots, and now paid once per process lifetime on the always-on host rather than on every cold start
RAG-specific logic: chunking pipeline, retriever, citation auditing, versioned prompt templates, curated dataset and its indexing script
embeddings example app logic: bundled preconfigured TextSample set, in-process embedding + PCA fit/transform, and the route accepting custom text and returning the recalculated 2D projection

single-call example app logic: bundled preset prompt set, per-preset Pydantic schema models for Structured mode, and the route returning a plain-text or structured (request+response) result via the shared generation service
chained-calls example app logic: PydanticAI agent setup, the two-step writer→critic run function with quote-overlap verification, and the route returning the intermediate and final outputs
versioned persona system-prompt templates ('struggling writer', 'harsh critic')

planning-agent example app logic: PydanticAI planner agent (structured-output Plan, validated and trimmed to the 2–3 step cap), Exa web-search tool registration for executor agents, the sequential user-advanced executor run function gated by the shared quota check, and the SSE route streaming Plan, StepResults and the final Itinerary
versioned planner and synthesis prompt templates with the Plan/StepResult/Itinerary structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside

ReAct loop example app logic: the typed multi-hop preset catalog (questions and hop metadata only, never answers), the moderation gate and suitability check for custom questions, the hand-rolled bounded reason-act-observe loop owning the cycle counter and search ceiling, the per-cycle typed thought/action call, the direct shared-Exa calls with verbatim snippets as observations, the worst-case allowance reservation and refund, the terminal-card selection, the post-run hop-source annotation, react_runs persistence, and the per-cycle SSE emission

the semantic near-duplicate query guard: embeds each candidate query via the shared embedding service, cosine-compares it against the run's already-issued query embeddings in an in-process NumPy array, and blocks a rephrased repeat before it spends a search; a pure function over (candidate, prior embeddings, threshold)
versioned ReAct prompt templates (cycle_v1.md, final_answer_v1.md, suitability_v1.md, hop_annotation_v1.md) with their structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside

orchestrated-subagents example app logic: the bundled four-specialist roster and curated presets, the moderation gate for free-form questions only, the coordinator agent producing a validated DelegationDecision, the asyncio.gather fan-out running the two specialists concurrently with return_exceptions=True, the merge call, the three-call budget reservation, and the SSE route
versioned coordinator delegation, specialist and merge prompt templates with their structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside

multi-agent collaboration example app logic: the opacity policy layer over the shared message bus, the deterministic RFQ composer that takes no model call, the buyer and two seller peer agents, the concurrent bid rounds, the counter-offer and award turns, the two post-award explanation calls, the eight-call budget reservation, and NegotiationRecord persistence plus per-stage SSE emission

the hand-rolled A2A-shaped Pydantic protocol models — AgentCard with AgentProvider/AgentSkill/AgentCapabilities, Task with TaskStatus/TaskState, Message with Role and Part/DataPart, and Artifact — serialised camelCase, in one readable file

typed Python literal fixtures, mypy-checked: the pre-tuned procurement scenario catalog, each scenario's per-seller sealed private constraints with their reveal headlines, the priority-weighting presets, and the three A2A-shaped agent identity cards
versioned negotiation prompt templates with the Bid/CounterOffer/Award and the two narrow explanation Pydantic schemas alongside
SQLAlchemy models, async session factory, and the Alembic migration tree targeting Neon
configuration (pydantic-settings), structlog and Sentry setup
pytest suites mirroring the package layout, including message-bus, collaboration-opacity and ReAct-loop invariant tests; live-provider tests are deselected by default

one folder per screen: landing, RAG example, tool-use example, embeddings example, single-call example, chained-calls example, planning-agent example, ReAct loop example, orchestrated-subagents example, multi-agent collaboration example, framework console
one folder per example app (rag, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning, react, orchestrated, collab, and future additions), each lazy-loaded via its own route
the embeddings example app's route module: plot component (react-plotly.js), custom-text input, and the educational explanation of the embedding pattern

the single-call example app's route module: prompt input and preset selector, Simple/Structured mode toggle, plain-text response view, side-by-side structured request/response JSON view, and the pattern explanation
the chained-calls example app's route module: initial-request input, upfront role description, labeled intermediate and final output blocks, the two-call quota notice, and the pattern explanation

the planning-agent example app's route module: city/interests input, plan display, the explicit 'Next' advance button, progressively appearing step results from the SSE stream, the final itinerary, the run-allowance display, the limit notices, and the pattern explanation cross-referencing the ReAct Loop example

the ReAct loop example app's route module: the educational overview, the five-preset selector and free-form input with its moderation/suitability messages, the start control with no plan display and no mid-run approval, the progressively filled cycle trace, the live cycle counter, the runs-remaining indicator, the two terminal cards, the hop-source annotation panel, and the exhausted state

the orchestrated-subagents example app's route module: preset selector and free-form input, the delegation-decision panel, the explicit 'Next' dispatch button, two parallel specialist columns with live independent status, the merged answer and disagreement note, the runs-remaining counter, the disabled-input state, and the pattern explanation

the multi-agent collaboration example app's route module: preset scenario selector and priority weighting (no free text), inspectable agent identity cards, the buyer track, two parallel seller columns with live status, the private-position reveal panel, the priority-sensitivity panel, the toggleable message log, the stated call cost, and the candid educational overview

the raw message-log view: a hand-rolled Tailwind-styled table with one row per envelope (sequence, time, sender → recipient, stage, summary) and expandable pretty-printed JSON work items, so the absence of any seller-to-seller row is visible at a glance
shared UI: nav bar, theme toggle, layout shell, and the shared markdown renderer wrapper around react-markdown with its Tailwind typography styles

typed API client and TanStack Query hooks calling the backend at same-origin /api/*, plus the SSE consumption hooks for the planning-agent, ReAct loop, orchestrated-subagents and multi-agent collaboration run streams
route configuration with lazy imports per example app, plus the SEO installer for per-route titles, descriptions and canonicals — canonicals now pointing at the single canonical VPS origin
Vitest + React Testing Library suites covering each example app's user-visible behaviour

patterns: functional core / imperative shell — pure functions for chunking/retrieval/scoring logic, PCA fit/transform, single-call schema validation, the chained-calls sequencing, the planning-agent plan validation and step sequencing, the orchestrated delegation validation, the moderation-response mapping, the ReAct duplicate guard, cycle-context assembly and terminal-card selection, and the collaboration app's deterministic RFQ composition, message-bus recipient filtering and opacity checks, with thin FastAPI route handlers as the imperative shell

dependency injection for shared services (LiteLLM client, PydanticAI agents, DB session, Exa client, embedding service, moderation service, peer message bus) via FastAPI's Depends, so tests can substitute them through app.dependency_overrides

concurrent agent work is dispatched in application code with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) rather than delegated to a model-driven tool loop, so call counts stay fixed and one worker's failure never cancels the other

iterative agent loops are likewise owned by application code, not by a framework's tool-calling iteration: the ReAct loop's cycle counter, search ceiling, duplicate guard and termination condition all live in the slice, so the call budget is a code invariant the allowance reservation can rely on
peer visibility is enforced structurally, never by prompt instruction: an agent's turn context is assembled only from envelopes the message bus returns for that agent
streaming routes open their own DB session inside the async generator via async_session_factory and never take a Depends(get_db_session), because the SSE response outlives the request handler

the backend runs as exactly one process with one Uvicorn worker: any state held in memory — the loaded embedding model, the fitted PCA projection, the peer message bus, the ReAct duplicate-guard cache — is per-process by design, so multi-worker or multi-instance deployment would silently break it

the FastAPI lifespan warm-up stays best-effort and idempotent: a failed embedding load or projection fit logs and boots anyway rather than taking the gallery down, moving the cost to the first request
secrets are read only from the environment (pydantic-settings) and never committed; on the VPS they live in a root-owned 0600 file referenced by the systemd unit, outside the repository tree
React: function components and hooks only, no class components
custom hooks for shared frontend logic (e.g. useExampleApps, useTheme, useRunAllowance)
documentation: Google-style docstrings on every public Python function
JSDoc on every exported TypeScript function
every source file, Python and TypeScript, opens with the header comment 'Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai'

unusually heavy explanatory comments stating why a decision was made — the deploy artifacts (Caddyfile, systemd unit, deploy script) follow the same convention, each documenting why the single-process, single-origin, warm-at-boot arrangement is what it is

additional_decisions.name: collaboration_run_call_budget
additional_decisions.description: The declared per-run model-call budget for the multi-agent collaboration example app, and how it is disclosed and policed.
additional_decisions.value: 8 calls per run, disclosed on the page as 6 negotiation calls (2 opening bids, 1 buyer counter, 2 best-and-final bids, 1 award) plus 2 post-award explanation calls (private-position reveal, priority sensitivity); all 8 reserved via allowance_holds before the deterministic RFQ is composed so a run is never begun that cannot complete; telemetry alerts on the negotiation-stage count differing from 6. Unchanged by this revision, which is behaviour-preserving with respect to every usage cap.

additional_decisions.name: react_run_call_budget
additional_decisions.description: The declared per-run model-call budget for the ReAct loop example app, and how it is reserved, disclosed and released.
additional_decisions.value: Worst case 10 calls per run, disclosed on the page as up to 8 search-cycle calls plus 1 final-answer call plus 1 post-run hop-source annotation call; the full worst case is reserved via allowance_holds before the first cycle and the unspent remainder refunded when the loop answers early. The custom-question suitability check is 1 further call charged only on free-form input. Unchanged by this revision.

additional_decisions.name: deployment_downtime_posture
additional_decisions.description: How a release interacts with the gallery's availability and warm-start goals, and the residual gap that was accepted.
additional_decisions.value: A release is a plain systemctl restart, so the gallery is briefly unavailable and the embedding model load plus PCA fit are re-paid at boot — a few seconds, borne by the deploy rather than by a visitor. Zero-downtime deployment (starting a second warm instance and switching Caddy's upstream) was considered and deliberately deferred as unnecessary machinery for a showcase that deploys infrequently; the goal of updating without interrupting visitors is therefore met by deploying rarely and quickly rather than by hot-swapping, and the two-process port flip remains an additive change if that ever chafes.

additional_decisions.name: retired_hosting_configuration
additional_decisions.description: What is removed from the repository as part of retiring the previous host.
additional_decisions.value: render.yaml is deleted from the repo root and the Render documentation reference is dropped from this spec; the previous host serves nothing after the cutover, and visitors reach the gallery only at the single canonical VPS origin. No environment variable is added, removed or renamed by the migration — the contract (DATABASE_URL, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, CORS_ORIGIN, optional SENTRY_DSN and VITE_SENTRY_DSN) carries over verbatim, relocated from the hosting dashboard to the systemd EnvironmentFile.

additional_decisions.name: frontend_lint_tooling_discrepancy
additional_decisions.description: A known divergence between this spec's recorded frontend linter/formatter and what the repository actually uses.
additional_decisions.value: This spec records ESLint + @typescript-eslint and Prettier for TypeScript, carried forward from earlier revisions, while the implemented repository lints with oxlint and has no ESLint and no Prettier installed. The discrepancy was surfaced during this revision and deliberately left unresolved, because re-deciding settled frontend tooling is outside a hosting migration's scope; a future revision that touches frontend tooling should reconcile the two, and until then the repository's oxlint setup is authoritative in practice.

additional_decisions.name: nfr_id_renaming_note
additional_decisions.description: Why satisfies_nfr ids differ between entries carried forward from earlier revisions and entries added or touched in this one.
additional_decisions.value: Successive revisions have renumbered the project-wide non-functional goal ids. Entries added or materially changed in a given revision are tagged with the ids current at that time; entries carried forward untouched retain the ids the previous implemented plan was built against, and were deliberately not re-tagged, since re-deciding settled entries is outside a revision's scope. This revision's new and changed entries — the deployment targets, the two new infrastructure entries, the embedding pipeline and projection cache, and the process supervision decision — use the current ids.
